parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
abide[abaid]v.
To abide by something, like a rule, means to obey it.
→ If you want to play the game with us, you must be willing to abide by our rules.
😎
conversion[kanva:rʒan]n.
Conversion is the act of changing something into a different state or form.
→ The city discussed the conversion of the parking lot into a skateboard park.
😎
cram[kræm]v.
To cram things means to put them into a place that can barely contain them.
→ He crammed all of his shirts into the top drawer of the dresser.
😎
defer[difair]v.
To defer means to arrange for an action to happen at a later time.
→ The girl was very sleepy, so she chose to defer her bath until morning.
😎
export[ikspo:rt]v.
To export products means to sell them to other countries.
→ The United States exports many cereals and grains.
😎
fume[fju:m]n.
Fumes are unhealthy smoke and gases that are made by fires or chemicals.
→ The engine put unpleasant, black fumes into the air.
😎
habitual[habitʃual]adj.
When something is habitual, it is a behavior that a person usually does or has.
→ The man was a habitual liar who was incapable of being honest with the police.
😎
justify[dʒʌstəfai]v.
To justify something means to show or prove that it is necessary.
→ The government tried to justify its decision to bring the country into a war.
😎
output[autput]n.
Output is the amount of something that a person or thing produces.
→ The boss hired more workers to increase the factory's output of products.
😎
overpopulation[ouvarpapjuleiʃan]n.
Overpopulation is the state of having too many people in an area.
→ The organization is concerned with overpopulation of the world.
😎
patent[pætant]n.
A patent is a right to be the only person allowed to make or sell a new product.
→ He quickly established a patent for his brilliant invention.
😎
penalize[pi:nǝlaiz]v.
To penalize someone means to punish him or her.
→ The team was penalized when they broke the rules.
😎
petroleum[pitrouliam]n.
Petroleum is a liquid natural resource from which many fuels are made.
→ The petroleum at that factory is used to make gasoline.
😎
prototype[proutataip]n.
A prototype is a new machine that is not ready to be made in large quantities.
→ He introduced his prototype to the motorcycle company.
😎
scrap[skræp]n.
A scrap of something is a small amount of it.
→ Chris liked to use many scraps of paper when thinking up ideas.
😎
sector[sektar]n.
A sector is a part of a country's economy in a specific type of industry.
→ We learned about just a few of the factories within the manufacturing sector.
😎
subscribe[sabskraib]v.
To subscribe to something is to agree or to concur with it.
→ She subscribed to the view that musical education should be kept in schools.
😎
subsist[sabsist]v.
To subsist means to have the food, water, and money needed to stay alive.
→ Some people are forced to subsist on only a few dollars a month.
😎
suspend[saspend]v.
To suspend something means to delay or stop it from happening for a while.
→ The oil company suspended production until it was sure the factory was safe.
😎
synthesis[sinθasis]n.
A synthesis is a combination of different ideas or styles.
→ The band's music was a synthesis of many different musical genres.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content:
The best theory was the one that was a combination of all the scientist’s ideas. [ 1 ]

When the power went out, he was forced to stop or delay progress on his project. [ 2 ]

The brothers believe along with other people to the opinion that socialism is best. [ 3 ]

The cutting tool was just a new machine not ready to be made in large amounts. [ 4 ]

Her job was to get all of the goods ready to sell to other countries. [ 5 ]

The chemist demonstrated the change into a different form of liquid water into gas. [ 6 ]

After the tornado, it was difficult for the family to have the food and money needed to live. [ 7 ]

The mechanic yelled when he stepped on the sharp small amount of metal. [ 8 ]

It is the policeman’s job to make sure people do what is right by the law. [ 9 ]

We’ll have to postpone our vacation until next month. [ 10 ]
questions.explanation: synthesis (n): a combination of different ideas or styles.
suspend (v): to delay or stop it from happening for a while.
subscribe (v): to agree or to concur with it.
prototype (n): a new machine that is not ready to be made in large quantities.
export (v): to sell products to other countries.
conversion (n): the act of changing something into a different state or form.
subsist (v): to have the food, water, and money needed to stay alive.
scrap (n): a small amount of it.
abide (v): to obey it.
defer (v): to arrange for an action to happen at a later time.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: The big city worked hard to prevent overpopulation problems.
questions.explanation: overpopulation (n): having too many people in an area.

questions.content: I tried to cram all of my clothes into one suitcase.
questions.explanation: cram (v): to put things into a place that can barely contain them.

questions.content: The machine’s output was so great that we ran out of room to store the products.
questions.explanation: output (n): the amount of something that a person or thing produces.

questions.content: Why don’t we defer the decision until right now?
questions.explanation: defer means to postpone to a later time, so 'until right now' is incorrect.

questions.content: The conversion over the bridge was scary.
questions.explanation: conversion means changing into a different state, which does not make sense here.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
Preparing for the Future

Overpopulation is a big problem in the world today. Too many people are crammed into cities and towns around the globe. Earth’s population is about 6.5 billion people. This number is growing every day. In just 50 years, the population will be almost 9 billion.

Many people worry that the Earth won’t have enough resources to support so many people. One major reason for this is that wasting resources and polluting have become habitual behaviors. Industrial output results in polluting the air with dangerous fumes. Also, cars and machines waste a ton of important natural resources like oil and water. It’s possible that the Earth may become so damaged that it cannot support a large population of humans.

Another issue is the lack of useful land for cultivating crops. Even today, many people subsist on mere scraps of food and little water. In 50 years, many experts worry that huge numbers of people will starve to death. So what is being done to prepare for the future?

People are realizing they can no longer justify their wasteful behavior or defer action to fix it. Many car companies already have patents on prototypes for very efficient cars. Such cars waste no resources and produce no pollution. A conversion to clean cars means that petroleum can be saved for the future. In addition, the environmental sectors of many governments are setting strict rules for industries that pollute too much. If companies do not abide by the standards, they are penalized with higher taxes. In some cases, their operations might be suspended altogether.

Food is also an issue that is being tackled. Many countries are now subscribing to the point of view that immediate action is needed. They are determining ways to export goods to people in need, so that no one goes hungry. Experts will continue to come up with ideas for the future, and a synthesis of these ideas will help to support the growing population.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: Because of overpopulation, too many people are crammed into cities and towns.
questions.explanation: Đúng. Đoạn 1 viết: "Overpopulation is a big problem... Too many people are crammed into cities and towns around the globe." (Bùng nổ dân số là một vấn đề lớn... Quá nhiều người bị nhồi nhét vào các thành phố và thị trấn trên toàn cầu).

questions.content: The environmental sectors of many governments are deferring strict standards.
questions.explanation: Sai. Đoạn 4 có câu: "...the environmental sectors of many governments are setting strict rules for industries that pollute too much." (các ban ngành môi trường của nhiều chính phủ đang đặt ra những quy định nghiêm ngặt đối với các ngành công nghiệp gây ô nhiễm quá mức). Họ đang thiết lập quy định, không phải đang trì hoãn (deferring) chúng.

questions.content: Some car companies have patents on prototypes.
questions.explanation: Đúng. Đoạn 4 viết: "Many car companies already have patents on prototypes for very efficient cars." (Nhiều công ty ô tô đã có bằng sáng chế về các nguyên mẫu cho những chiếc xe hơi rất tiết kiệm nhiên liệu).

questions.content: A conversion to clean cars means petroleum can be used right now for people.
questions.explanation: Sai. Đoạn 4 giải thích: "A conversion to clean cars means that petroleum can be saved for the future." (Việc chuyển đổi sang ô tô sạch đồng nghĩa với việc dầu mỏ có thể được tiết kiệm cho tương lai). Chứ không phải được sử dụng ngay bây giờ (right now).

questions.content: Companies that don’t abide by standards are penalized or their operations might be suspended.
questions.explanation: Đúng. Đoạn 4 có viết: "If companies do not abide by the standards, they are penalized with higher taxes. In some cases, their operations might be suspended altogether." (Nếu các công ty không tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn, họ sẽ bị trừng phạt bằng mức thuế cao hơn. Trong một số trường hợp, hoạt động của họ có thể bị đình chỉ hoàn toàn).

questions.content: What will a synthesis of good ideas for the future do?
options: A synthesis of these ideas will help to support the growing population.
questions.explanation: Câu cuối của bài đọc ghi: "...a synthesis of these ideas will help to support the growing population." (...sự tổng hợp của những ý tưởng này sẽ giúp nuôi sống dân số đang ngày một tăng). Đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: What have become habitual behaviors in the world today?
options: Wasting resources and polluting have become habitual behaviors in the world today.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2 giải thích: "One major reason for this is that wasting resources and polluting have become habitual behaviors." (Một nguyên nhân lớn dẫn đến điều này là việc lãng phí tài nguyên và gây ô nhiễm đã trở thành những hành vi theo thói quen). Do đó đáp án A là đúng.

questions.content: What prototypes do companies have patents for in the passage?
options: Many car companies already have patents on prototypes for very efficient cars.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4 có viết: "Many car companies already have patents on prototypes for very efficient cars." (Nhiều công ty ô tô đã có bằng sáng chế về các nguyên mẫu cho những chiếc xe hơi rất tiết kiệm nhiên liệu). Vậy đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: What behavior can no longer be justified?
options: People are realizing they can no longer justify their wasteful behavior.
questions.explanation: Đầu đoạn 4 nêu: "People are realizing they can no longer justify their wasteful behavior..." (Mọi người đang nhận ra rằng họ không thể tiếp tục biện minh cho hành vi lãng phí của mình...). Do đó đáp án A là đúng.

questions.content: What point of view are many countries subscribing to?
options: Immediate action is needed to provide the world with enough food.
They should cram more people into cities.
questions.explanation: Đoạn cuối có viết: "Many countries are now subscribing to the point of view that immediate action is needed." (Hiện nay nhiều quốc gia đang đồng tình với quan điểm rằng cần phải hành động ngay lập tức). Đáp án A là chính xác.
